name: Nick Swinmurn
milestone_by_age_26: Founded Zappos (initially Shoesite.com) in 1999 at about age 26, creating what became a leading online shoe retailer later acquired by Amazon.
early_history_summary: Born in England and moved to the U.S. Bay Area at age seven; father was an engineer and mother a teacher. Graduated UCSB in film studies (1995), worked in sports ticket sales and at Autoweb.com, then left in 1998 to pursue an online shoe store after struggling to find shoes in a San Francisco mall.
family_context_summary: Born in England; moved to the Bay Area at seven. Father worked as an engineer; mother was a teacher.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were not in retail or e-commerce; no clear industry apprenticeship documented.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Bay Area, e-commerce wave, Autoweb exposure, later Hsieh partnership
evidence_summary: Swinmurn founded Zappos in 1999 after a personal shopping frustration and early internet-startup exposure at Autoweb. Family background is middle-class professional (engineer father, teacher mother) without retail inheritance. Later partnered with Tony Hsieh/Venture Frogs; left Zappos in 2006 before Amazon's acquisition. Advantage stack is moderate: geography and market timing more than elite pedigree.
starting_point: Born in England ~1973; relocated to the California Bay Area at age seven; father an engineer, mother a teacher; film studies at UCSB.
current_position: Entrepreneur and investor; founder of Basecamp Fitness (later acquired); minority investor in Golden State Warriors and Leeds United ownership groups.

trajectory.event: Graduated UCSB with a film studies degree; later worked in baseball ticket sales and at Autoweb.com.
Founded Zappos (Shoesite.com), pioneering large-selection online shoe retail.
Tony Hsieh / Venture Frogs invested; Hsieh joined leadership and elevated customer-service culture.
Left Zappos while retaining equity before the company's peak scale.
Amazon acquired Zappos in a stock deal valued around $1.2 billion.
Founded Basecamp Fitness, later acquired by Self Esteem Brands.

name: Jason Citron
milestone_by_age_26: Founded OpenFeint in 2009 (age ~24-25), building a major mobile social gaming network that sold to GREE in 2011 for ~$104M when he was 26.
early_history_summary: Born in San Francisco (Sept 21, 1984), raised partly in South Florida; learned QBasic at 13 after receiving a computer from his grandfather. Earned a B.S. in Game Design from Full Sail University (2004), then founded OpenFeint during the early App Store wave before later co-founding Discord.
family_context_summary: Born in San Francisco to a family with some business/technology background; grew up in South Florida. Grandfather gifted him an early computer.
parent_family_domain_summary: Family had business/technology background per secondary sources, but no clear mobile-gaming industry dynasty documented.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early coding, game design degree, App Store wave, gaming community immersion
evidence_summary: Citron coded as a teen, specialized in game design at Full Sail, and rode the iPhone App Store wave with OpenFeint—sold for ~$104M at age 26. Later co-founded Discord (2015) after building Hammer & Chisel. Family advantage is lightly documented; primary path was product skill plus platform timing rather than inherited capital.
starting_point: Born San Francisco 1984; raised with early computer access via grandfather; game-design education at Full Sail (graduated 2004).
current_position: Co-founder and former CEO of Discord; stepped down as CEO in April 2025, remaining on the board; Discord last valued around $15B (2021 round).

trajectory.event: Graduated Full Sail University with a B.S. in Game Design and Development.
Founded OpenFeint, a leading mobile social gaming platform for the iPhone App Store era.
Sold OpenFeint to GREE for approximately $104 million.
Publicly launched Discord after pivoting Hammer & Chisel from a game studio to chat infrastructure.
Discord raised at a ~$15 billion valuation amid rapid pandemic-era growth.
Stepped down as Discord CEO; Humam Sakhnini succeeded him while Citron remained on the board.

name: Stanislav Vishnevskiy
milestone_by_age_26: Founded Guildwork (Guild Work) around 2009 at about age 22, building MMO guild management tools that established him as a gaming infrastructure engineer before co-founding Discord.
early_history_summary: Born in Ukraine and immigrated to the U.S. at age five; learned programming through online games and community tooling. Built eqDKP and Guildwork for MMO guilds, then joined Jason Citron at Hammer & Chisel (2013) and co-founded Discord (2015) as CTO.
family_context_summary: Ukrainian immigrant to the U.S. at age five; detailed family financial or professional background not well documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: MMO community, self-taught engineering, Guildwork, Citron partnership
evidence_summary: Vishnevskiy self-taught via online games, shipped Guildwork for MMO guilds by his early twenties, then partnered with Jason Citron to build Discord. Immigrant outsider path with strong domain immersion and complementary cofounder pairing; family wealth/networks not documented. Discord co-founding (2015) came at ~28, after the <=26 Guildwork milestone.
starting_point: Born in Ukraine (~1987); immigrated to the U.S. at age five; formed identity and skills through online gaming communities.
current_position: CTO and co-founder of Discord; remains a core technical leader of the company after Citron stepped down as CEO in 2025.

trajectory.event: Founded Guildwork, tooling for MMO guilds that built his reputation in gaming infrastructure.
Joined Jason Citron at Hammer & Chisel to work on multiplayer games and chat systems.
Co-founded and publicly launched Discord as CTO.
Discord broadened beyond gaming; user growth surged during the pandemic.
Discord raised capital at a multi-billion-dollar valuation as a mainstream community platform.

name: Kevin Lin
milestone_by_age_26: No material founder milestone by age 26 clearly documented. Born 1982 (Yale ecology/evolutionary biology); Twitch brand launch ~2011 (~age 29) and Amazon acquisition 2014 (~age 32). Classic Justin.tv founding quartet is typically listed as Kan/Shear/Seibel/Vogt; Lin is widely described as Twitch co-founder/COO associated with the later gaming pivot.
early_history_summary: Born in New Orleans in 1982; graduated Yale with a degree in Ecology and Evolutionary Biology. Became a longtime Justin.tv/Twitch operator and COO, helping scale Twitch before Amazon’s ~$970M acquisition, then founded Metatheory and co-founded Gold House.
family_context_summary: Born in New Orleans; detailed family financial/professional background not documented in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Kevin Lin’s widely cited milestones (Twitch gaming brand ~2011, Amazon acquisition 2014, later Metatheory) occur after age 26. Without a dated <=26 material founding event supported by two sources, he is coded ineligible under the strict age rule.

name: Anthony Levandowski
milestone_by_age_26: Led Berkeley Blue Team’s autonomous motorcycle Ghostrider into the 2004 DARPA Grand Challenge at age 24 (also competed 2005), after earlier student companies including La Raison as a teen/freshman.
early_history_summary: Born March 15, 1980 in Brussels to a French diplomat mother and American businessman; moved to California mid-1990s. Built websites as a teen, founded La Raison (~1997-98), won a Lego robotics contest as a Berkeley sophomore, and led the Ghostrider autonomous motorcycle project for DARPA before Google Street View and Waymo work.
family_context_summary: Born in Brussels to a French diplomat mother and American businessman; later lived in Marin County, California. Bought a house young with some parental help from father/stepmother per 2003 Berkeley profile.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother worked for the European Union in Belgium; father was a businessman—adjacent professional resources but not a robotics dynasty.
primary_early_advantage_tags: UC Berkeley, early entrepreneurship, DARPA, Bay Area robotics, La Raison profits
evidence_summary: Levandowski combined teenage entrepreneurship (La Raison), Berkeley engineering, and DARPA-era autonomous vehicle building by his mid-twenties. Ghostrider (2004-05) is a clear <=26 material milestone later housed in the Smithsonian. Subsequent Google/Waymo/Otto career defined self-driving’s first commercial wave, alongside major legal controversy and a 2021 presidential pardon.
starting_point: Born Brussels 1980 to a French diplomat mother and American businessman; moved to California as a teen; early web businesses in Marin/Berkeley.
current_position: CEO of Pronto (autonomous systems, including off-road/mining pivot); serial self-driving entrepreneur after Google/Waymo, Otto/Uber, and legal battles.

trajectory.event: Entered UC Berkeley; already running La Raison intranet/IT services founded as a teen.
Launched Construction Control Systems / WorkTop portable blueprint reader while a Berkeley grad student.
Led Ghostrider autonomous motorcycle team in the first DARPA Grand Challenge.
Joined Google mapping/Street View effort with Sebastian Thrun after DARPA work.
Co-founded Google’s self-driving car project (later Waymo).
Left Google to co-found Otto; Uber acquired Otto later that year.
Received a full presidential pardon after trade-secret conviction; later returned as Pronto CEO.

name: Chris Urmson
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. BSc University of Manitoba 1998 (~22); PhD CMU 2005 (~29). DARPA Grand Challenge technical leadership 2004-05 (~28-29) and Urban Challenge win 2007 (~31); Google self-driving leadership from 2009; Aurora founded 2017 (~41).
early_history_summary: Canadian-born 1976 to English emigrant parents; moved across Canada as a child. Computer engineering at Manitoba, then CMU robotics PhD; became a core DARPA and Google self-driving leader before founding Aurora.
family_context_summary: Son of English emigrants in Canada; father worked for Correctional Service of Canada and later became warden of Kent Institution.
parent_family_domain_summary: No robotics/self-driving domain advantage documented; father in corrections administration.
evidence_summary: Urmson’s defining public milestones are post-26 (DARPA 2004+ at ~28+, Google AV leadership, Aurora). Education by 26 alone does not meet the material-milestone bar.

name: Sebastian Thrun
milestone_by_age_26: No material professional milestone by age 26 found. Born May 14, 1967; Vordiplom ~1988 (~21); Diplom University of Bonn 1993 (~26) and PhD 1995 (~28). Career breakthroughs (CMU faculty, Minerva, Stanford SAIL, DARPA Grand Challenge win 2005, Google X/Waymo, Udacity) all post-26.
early_history_summary: Born Solingen, West Germany; studied CS/economics/medicine then CS at Bonn under Armin Cremers with Tom Mitchell as co-advisor. Academic robotics career at CMU and Stanford preceded Google X, Waymo, Udacity, and Kitty Hawk.
family_context_summary: Born to Winfried and Kristin (Grüner) Thrun in Solingen; further family socioeconomic detail limited in reviewed sources.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources as AI/robotics domain expertise.
evidence_summary: Thrun’s global fame (DARPA 2005, Google X, Udacity MOOCs) is well after age 26. A Diplom at ~26 is academic progress, not a material public/commercial breakthrough under the rubric.

name: Luis von Ahn
milestone_by_age_26: Co-created CAPTCHA with Manuel Blum and collaborators around 2000 (published early 2000s) at about age 21-22 while a young CMU researcher, inventing a widely deployed human-vs-bot verification method.
early_history_summary: Born August 19, 1978 in Guatemala City; raised by a single mother who was one of Guatemala’s early women physicians. Received a Commodore 64 at eight, attended American School of Guatemala, earned summa cum laude math B.S. from Duke (2000), then CMU PhD (2005) under Manuel Blum, inventing CAPTCHA, ESP Game, reCAPTCHA, and later Duolingo.
family_context_summary: Raised in Guatemala City by a single mother who finished medical school and gave birth at 42; German descent on father’s side. Family could fund private English-language schooling and a childhood computer.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother was a physician; not a CS/tech industry transfer, but strong educational emphasis and resources relative to local context.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Manuel Blum, Duke, CMU, early computer, CAPTCHA research, Guatemala-to-US education path
evidence_summary: Von Ahn’s CAPTCHA work by ~22 is a textbook <=26 technical milestone, later compounded by reCAPTCHA (sold to Google), MacArthur Fellowship (2006), and Duolingo. Advantage mix is elite CS mentorship/institutions plus a privileged educational platform in Guatemala, not inherited tech wealth. Duolingo made him a global consumer-tech CEO.
starting_point: Born Guatemala City 1978; raised by a single-mother physician; private English schooling and childhood Commodore 64; left for Duke at 18.
current_position: Co-founder and CEO of Duolingo (public company); also joined Figma’s board in 2025; major education-tech and human-computation figure.

trajectory.event: Graduated Duke summa cum laude in mathematics; early CAPTCHA research with Manuel Blum underway.
Published foundational CAPTCHA cryptographic/HCI work that entered wide web deployment.
Completed CMU PhD on human computation; thesis coined and formalized the research program.
Awarded MacArthur Fellowship; joined CMU faculty.
Google acquired reCAPTCHA; began developing Duolingo with Severin Hacker.
Duolingo released publicly after private beta.
Duolingo IPO; von Ahn continued as CEO of a large public language-learning platform.

name: Severin Hacker
milestone_by_age_26: Began co-creating Duolingo with advisor Luis von Ahn around 2009 at about age 24-25 during his CMU PhD, founding the company that became the world’s largest language-learning app (company formalization often dated 2011).
early_history_summary: Born November 6, 1984 in Zug, Switzerland; drawn to CS via video games. Earned B.S. from ETH Zurich (2006) and Ph.D. from CMU (2014) under Luis von Ahn; co-founded Duolingo as CTO while a graduate student.
family_context_summary: Born and raised in Zug, Switzerland; detailed parental occupations not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: ETH Zurich, CMU PhD, Luis von Ahn advisor-cofounder, gamification ML
evidence_summary: Hacker paired elite European CS training with a high-trust advisor relationship that became a cofounder partnership. Duolingo’s origin during his PhD (2009-2011) at ages ~24-26 is the <=26 milestone; public launch and scale came later. Institutional pipelines and mentorship dominate over family-domain inheritance.
starting_point: Born Zug, Switzerland 1984; gaming-driven path into CS; ETH Zurich undergrad then CMU PhD under Luis von Ahn.
current_position: Co-founder, CTO, and board director of Duolingo; long-running technical partner to CEO Luis von Ahn.

trajectory.event: Completed B.S. in computer science at ETH Zurich.
Began co-developing Duolingo with advisor Luis von Ahn at CMU.
Duolingo company founding period; TechCrunch covered the product as an emerging language platform.
Duolingo publicly launched after private beta.
Completed CMU Ph.D.; recognized among MIT TR35 innovators.
Duolingo IPO; Hacker continued as CTO and board member.

name: Daniel Weinand
milestone_by_age_26: Joined Tobias Lütke and Scott Lake in 2005 (~age 26) to co-found the Shopify platform that publicly launched in 2006, after their Snowdevil online store work.
early_history_summary: Born in Germany (often cited May 26, 1979); studied computer science and music at University of Dortmund; self-taught designer/photographer. Co-founded Shopify in Ottawa with Lütke and Lake, serving long-term as design/culture leader through IPO era.
family_context_summary: Born in Germany; detailed parental occupations and wealth not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Lütke partnership, design craft, Snowdevil-to-Shopify, Ottawa startup cluster
evidence_summary: Weinand’s <=26 milestone is co-founding Shopify’s platform build in 2005 (launch 2006) with Lütke after Snowdevil. Primary edge was complementary design/product partnership on the e-commerce software wave rather than elite pedigree or family capital. Later CDO/culture roles and exit from day-to-day operations after scale.
starting_point: Born in Germany ~1979; CS/music studies at University of Dortmund; self-taught design/photography path into Canadian tech.
current_position: Shopify co-founder; former Chief Design Officer / Chief Culture Officer; later focused on investing, creative work, and independent projects after leaving full-time executive roles.

trajectory.event: Joined Lütke and Lake to co-found/build the Shopify platform after Snowdevil.
Shopify platform launched publicly as multi-merchant e-commerce software.
Became Chief Design Officer, shaping Shopify’s product aesthetic and merchant UX.
Shopify IPO; Weinand remained a core design/culture executive.
Transitioned away from full-time C-suite operational roles after long tenure.

name: Danny Postma
milestone_by_age_26: No clearly material, widely verified milestone by age 26. Launched Landingfolio ~2015 (~age 21-23) as an early design gallery project, but the first clearly material success documented in secondary sources is Headlime’s ~7-figure acquisition (~2020, age ~28) and later HeadshotPro (~2023).
early_history_summary: Dutch indie maker who taught himself product/design/code; built a portfolio of micro-SaaS and AI tools (Landingfolio, Headlime, HeadshotPro) often while based in Bali. Known for bootstrapped AI products reaching high MRR without traditional VC.
evidence_summary: Postma’s breakout economic milestones (Headlime exit, HeadshotPro scale) are documented after age 26. Early Landingfolio is a starter product but lacks strong dual-sourced evidence as a material career-defining milestone by 26 under a conservative reading.
